# The Context


## Where does the data come from?

**"Travel Reviews" dataset**

<div style="margin-top: 10%; font-size: 75%; line-height: 1.8;">
- Official source: UCI Machine Learning Repository (University of California).
- Data source: extracted (crawled) from the TripAdvisor.com website.
- Authors: Shini Renjith, A. Sreekumar, and M. Jathavedan (2018).
- Geographical context: destinations located in East Asia.

# The Exploration


## Key indicators

```{r, comment = ""}

# 1. Creating a table summarising the data (minimum, maximum, median, mean, quantiles, standard deviations)

  # Calculate each statistic separately for all columns
mins    <- sapply(tripadvisor, min)
q1s     <- sapply(tripadvisor, quantile, probs = 0.25)
medians <- sapply(tripadvisor, median)
means   <- sapply(tripadvisor, mean)
q3s     <- sapply(tripadvisor, quantile, probs = 0.75)
maxs    <- sapply(tripadvisor, max)
sds     <- sapply(tripadvisor, sd)
  # Compile all the data into a data frame
tableau_resume <- data.frame(
  Minimum = mins,
  Q1 = q1s,
  Median = medians,
  Mean = means,
  Q3 = q3s,
  Maximum = maxs,
  SD = sds
)
  # Round the figures so that they are easy to read (to two decimal places)
tableau_resume <- round(tableau_resume, 2)

  # Display the result in the console
print(tableau_resume)
```


# The structure


## Cleaning 
<div style="display: flex; align-items: center;">
<div style="margin-top: 0% ; font-size: 75%">
- **The findings**
<br>

The standard deviation ($\sigma$) of the variable *Parks* is **`r sd(tripadvisor$Parks)`**. It is a virtually constant variable.
<br>

- **The mathematical danger**
<br>

The PCA standardises the data using the following formula:
$$Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma}$$
<br>

- **The "distorting magnifying glass" effect**
<br>

Dividing by **`r sd(tripadvisor$Parks)`** is equivalent to **multiplying by `r round(1/sd(tripadvisor$Parks), 0)`**.
Even the slightest micro-variation (noise) in *Parks* would have taken on disproportionate significance relative to the other variables, obscuring the actual structure of the data.
<br>
</div>

```{r}
# 1. Preparing the data

  # Remove "Parks" from the dataset as its variance is zero
tripadvisor2 <- tripadvisor[, colnames(tripadvisor) != "Parks"]
```


## How many axes are required?
<div style="display: flex; align-items: center;">
<div style="margin-top: 0% ; font-size: 75%">
**Simplification** to summarise the reality as accurately as possible.

```{r}

# 2. Calculating PCA (dudi.pca)

  # Display, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE : standardised PCA
trip_acp <- dudi.pca(tripadvisor2, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE, scannf = FALSE, nf = 5)


# 3. Principal component analysis: how much information does it provide?

  # Calculating percentages
eig_val <- trip_acp$eig
eig_pct <- round(eig_val / sum(eig_val) * 100, 1)

  # PLOT OF SCREENING MATERIAL
    # Graphical window
par(mfrow=c(1, 1), mar=c(5, 5, 4, 2))
    # Display
bp <- barplot(eig_pct, 
        names.arg = paste0("Axis ", 1:length(eig_pct)),
        main = "Cascade of eigenvalues",
        ylab = "% variance",
        col = "#505050",
        ylim = c(0, 110))
    # Adding points and lines for cumulative variance
cumexpvar<-round(cumsum(trip_acp$eig/sum(trip_acp$eig)*100),0)
lines(bp,cumexpvar,col ="#e78ac3")
points(bp,cumexpvar,col ="#e78ac3")
text(x = bp, 
     y = cumexpvar, 
     labels = paste0(round(cumexpvar, 0), "%"), 
     pos = 3,       
     cex = 0.8,    
     col = "#e78ac3", 
     font = 2)
```


## The DNA of the axes
<div style="display: flex; align-items: center;">
<div style="margin-top: 0% ; font-size: 75%">
**Weight** of each variable in the **construction** of the axis.

```{r, comment = ""}
  # Table of contributions
    # Calculation of contributions
contrib_var <- trip_acp$co^2
for(i in 1:5) {
  contrib_var[,i] <- (contrib_var[,i] / trip_acp$eig[i]) * 100
}
    # Rounding 
tableau_arrondi <- round(contrib_var[, 1:5], 2)
    # Creating a table
tableau_final <- as.data.frame(lapply(tableau_arrondi, function(x) paste0(x, " %")))
    # Naming lines (activities) that disappear with lapply
rownames(tableau_final) <- rownames(contrib_var)
    # Display of the results
print(tableau_final)
    # Calculating mean
moyennes_calculees <- colMeans(tableau_arrondi) 
    # Rounding and adding the %
moyenne_tableau <- as.data.frame(t(paste0(round(moyennes_calculees, 2), " %")))
    # Naming of columns
colnames(moyenne_tableau) <- colnames(tableau_arrondi)
    # Naming the line
rownames(moyenne_tableau) <- "Limit"
    # Display
print(moyenne_tableau)
```

# The Segmentation


## The judge of our segmentation
<div style="margin-top: 0% ; font-size: 75%">
**Measuring** the actual **quality** of the cut.

```{r}
# 1. How many clusters ?

 # Silhouette method
    # Parameters
k.max <- 10
Silhouette <- rep(0, k.max)
for(i in 2:k.max){
  km.res <- kmeans(tripadvisor, centers = i, nstart = 25)
  ss <- silhouette(km.res$cluster, dist(tripadvisor))
  Silhouette[i] <- mean(ss[, 3])
}
    # Display
plot(1:k.max, Silhouette, type = "b", pch = 19, 
     frame = FALSE, xlab = "Number of clusters k", main="Number of optimal clusters")
abline(v = which.max(Silhouette), lty = 2, col = "#e78ac3")
```


## Market shares
<div style="margin-top: 0% ; font-size: 75%">
**Allocation** determining how we distribute our **resources**.

```{r, comment = ""}
# 2. Hierarchical clustering of our individuals
     
  # Hierarchical clustering of the dataset excluding "Parks"
distances <- dist(scale(tripadvisor2), method = "euclidean")
clustering_i <- hclust(distances, method = "ward.D2")
groupes_2 <- cutree(clustering_i, k = 2)
comptage_voyageurs <- table(groupes_2)

  # Table of ratings mean
groupes_finaux <- cutree(clustering_i, k = 2)
profils <- aggregate(tripadvisor2, by = list(Cluster = groupes_finaux), FUN = mean)
rownames(profils) <- paste("Group", profils$Cluster)
profils <- profils[, -1] 
ligne_ecart <- abs(profils[1, ] - profils[2, ])
tableau_final <- rbind(profils, Difference = ligne_ecart)
tableau_final <- round(tableau_final, 2)
print(tableau_final)

  # PIECHART
    # Graphical window
par(mfrow=c(2, 1), mar=c(1.5, 1, 2, 1)) 
    # Display
pie(comptage_voyageurs, 
    main = "",
    col = c("#e78ac3", "#505050"), 
    labels = paste("Group", names(comptage_voyageurs), ":", comptage_voyageurs, "travelers"))
```

## Supply Strategy
<div style="margin-top: 0% ; font-size: 75%">
Selling **ecosystems** rather than 9 **isolated** products.

```{r}
# 3. Hierarchical clustering of our activities

  # Clustering of the transpose of the dataset excluding "Parks"
distances <- dist(t(tripadvisor2), method = "euclidian")
clustering_a <- hclust(distances, method = "ward.D2")

  # DENDOGRAM
    # Margins
par(mar=c(5, 4, 4, 2))
    # Display
plot(clustering_a, 
     main = "Similarities between activities",
     xlab = "", 
     ylab = "",
     sub = "",
     hang = -1,
     col = "black",
     lwd = 2)
      # Adding of a box to separate the groups
rect.hclust(clustering_a, k = 3, border = "#e78ac3")
```


# Conclusion


## New structure of the supply
<div style="display: flex; align-items: center;">
<div style="margin-top: 0% ; font-size: 75%">
- **The supply strategy**
<br>

The activities are therefore not **independent**, 3 **consumer ecosystems** have been identified:

1. The *free & spiritual* package
2. The *overnight stay & accommodation* package
3. The *culture & tasting* package
<br>

- **Involvement**
<br>

Any marketing strategy that attempts to sell a product from the *first pack* to a customer looking for the *second pack* is doomed to failure (the mathematical distance is too great).
<br>

- **The targeting strategy**
<br>

The divide here lies in the use of services, with **absolute priority** given to the group using toll infrastructure.
<br>
</div>


## Recommandations 

<div style="display: flex; align-items: center;">
<div style="margin-top: 0% ; font-size: 75%">
- **Tripadvisor**
<br>

The current algorithm often suggests *popular activities nearby* without ensuring consistency.\
The **opportunity** presented by this analysis is to move from a geographical recommendation to a **semantic recommendation**.
<br>

- **Local stakeholders**
<br>

They won’t be able to please everyone.\
**Partnerships** (B2B) must be established on this same **semantic** basis.
<br>

- **Investors**
<br>

80% of the budget must be allocated to the paid-activity consumer group.\
Funding large **integrated complexes** is one way of capturing the **customer base** of these individuals.
</div>
